goal: Codex intelligent model selection research refresh
refresh_summary: First durable research-bank capture for Codex model tiering. This refresh resolves the roadmap gap around T-015, preserves the current OpenAI model-family evidence, and sharpens the architecture direction toward alias- and capability-based selection with separate reasoning-effort policy rather than hard-coded tier mappings.
limitations: OpenAI model availability, alias behavior, pricing, and product positioning are temporally unstable; the external findings were refreshed against official sources observed on 2026-04-22.
Repo-local findings describe the current root-azoth snapshot only and may age as selector plumbing, deploy surfaces, or Codex host behavior change.
This capsule is planning-grade evidence for T-015. It does not authorize runtime selector implementation or automatic changes to spawned model behavior.

questions.question: Can this Codex model-tiering research capsule be reused for the next T-015 planning or proposal pass?
What is the lowest-friction forward-compatible architecture for Codex model tiering in Azoth?

thesis: Azoth should hard-code the selector contract, not the chosen models. The stable surface remains portable `model_tier` plus a small set of selector hints; Codex then resolves those hints through one host-local inventory/policy artifact that maps capability classes to preferred aliases and fallback aliases, while resolving `reasoning_effort` separately from model choice.

decisions_locked.contract_shape: portable intent plus host-local selector policy
decisions_locked.forward_compatibility_strategy: aliases and capability classes, not pinned snapshots or one tier-to-one-model mapping
decisions_locked.reasoning_policy_shape: resolve reasoning_effort separately from model alias
decisions_locked.queue_position: planned phase-3 follow-on under INI-PLT-006, not current active implementation work

repo_findings: T-015 already existed as a spec and draft architecture proposal, but this worktree was missing the live backlog row and INI-PLT-006 roadmap slice needed to make that planning seed valid.

The current orchestrator and subagent-router contracts say the orchestrator sets `model_tier` and a resolver chooses a concrete model later, but the resolver is not actually implemented in repo-local Codex surfaces.
The current Codex deploy path only projects an optional static `model` field into `.codex/agents/*.toml`; it does not project a selector policy artifact or a separate `reasoning_effort` contract.
The active `v0.2.0-p3` queue intentionally contains only the Karpathy slices, so T-015 should be represented as a planned INI-PLT-006 follow-on rather than forced into the live implementation queue.

sources.title: Models guide
sources.published_context: Official OpenAI API models guide observed on 2026-04-22
findings: OpenAI currently recommends `gpt-5.4` as the default starting point for complex reasoning and coding.
`gpt-5.4-mini` is positioned as a lower-latency frontier variant and supports the same reasoning-effort ladder as `gpt-5.4`.
The current model catalog already favors alias-based references over snapshot-specific contracts for general use.

sources.title: GPT-5.4 mini model docs
sources.published_context: Official OpenAI model page observed on 2026-04-22
findings: OpenAI currently describes `gpt-5.4-mini` as its strongest mini for coding, computer use, and subagents.
That positioning makes `gpt-5.4-mini` a strong default leaf-worker candidate without making the model name itself the long-term contract.

sources.title: GPT-5.3-Codex model docs
sources.published_context: Official OpenAI model page observed on 2026-04-22
findings: OpenAI currently describes `gpt-5.3-codex` as the most capable agentic coding model.
The page explicitly documents `low`, `medium`, `high`, and `xhigh` reasoning-effort settings, which supports a selector that chooses model alias and reasoning effort separately.

sources.title: Introducing GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark
sources.published_context: OpenAI product post published 2026-02-12 and observed on 2026-04-22
findings: Codex-Spark is currently framed as a real-time coding lane optimized for latency-sensitive iteration.
OpenAI explicitly says its default working style stays lightweight and targeted, including not automatically running tests unless asked.
That makes Codex-Spark a bounded latency-first leaf option rather than a good default for the main Azoth control plane.

recommended_reuse_for: forward-compatible model and reasoning policy discussions
